# Ecclesiastes Chapter 3 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**3:1** To-everything [la-kol] [there is] a-season [zeman], and-a-time [ve-et] to-every matter [le-khol chefetz] under the-heavens:

**3:2** A-time to-bear [la-ledet] and-a-time to-die [la-mut]; a-time to-plant [la-ta'at] and-a-time to-uproot [la'aqor] what-is-planted [natu'a]. **3:3** A-time to-kill [la-harog] and-a-time to-heal [li-rpo']; a-time to-break-down [li-frotz] and-a-time to-build-up [li-vnot]. **3:4** A-time to-weep [li-vkot] and-a-time to-laugh [li-sechoq]; a-time to-mourn [se-fod] and-a-time to-dance [re-qod]. **3:5** A-time to-cast-away [le-hashlikh] stones [avanim] and-a-time to-gather [ke-nos] stones; a-time to-embrace [la-chavoq] and-a-time to-refrain [li-rchoq] from-embracing [me-chabeq]. **3:6** A-time to-seek [le-vaqesh] and-a-time to-lose [le-abed]; a-time to-keep [li-shmor] and-a-time to-cast-away [le-hashlikh]. **3:7** A-time to-tear [li-qro'a] and-a-time to-sew [li-tpor]; a-time to-be-silent [la-chashot] and-a-time to-speak [le-daber]. **3:8** A-time to-love [le-ehov] and-a-time to-hate [li-sno']; a-time of-war [milchamah] and-a-time of-peace [shalom].

**3:9** What profit [yitron] [has] the-worker [ha-oseh] in-that which he toils?

**3:10** I-saw the-task [ha-inyan] that God has-given to-the-sons of-the-human to-be-occupied [la'anot] with-it. **3:11** The-all [et-ha-kol] he-has-made beautiful [yafeh] in-its-time [be-itto]; also the-eternity [ha-olam] he-has-set [natan] in-their-heart [be-libbam], except-that [mi-beli asher] the-human [ha-adam] cannot find-out [lo yimtza] the-work [ha-ma'aseh] that God has-done from-the-beginning [me-rosh] to-the-end [ve-ad-sof].

**3:12** I-knew that-there-is-nothing [ein] good [tov] in-them except to-rejoice [li-smoach] and-to-do good [la'asot tov] in-his-life [be-chayyav]. **3:13** And-also every human [kol ha-adam] who-eats and-drinks and-sees [ve-ra'ah] good in-all his-toil — it [is] a-gift [mattat] of-God.

**3:14** I-knew that all that God does — it will-be to-forever [le-olam]; upon-it there-is-nothing to-add [le-hosif], and-from-it there-is-nothing to-subtract [li-gro'a]. And-God has-done [it] so-that [she-] they-should-fear [yire'u] before-him [mi-le-fanav].

**3:15** What has-been [mah she-hayah] already [kevar] is [hu], and-what is-to-be [la-heyot] already has-been; and-God seeks [mevaqesh] the-pursued [et-nirdaf].

**3:16** And-moreover [ve-od] I-saw under the-sun: the-place [meqom] of-justice [ha-mishpat] — there [was] the-wickedness [ha-resha]; and-the-place of-righteousness [ha-tzedeq] — there [was] the-wickedness.

**3:17** I-said, I, in-my-heart, "The-righteous [et-ha-tzaddiq] and-the-wicked [ve-et-ha-rasha] God will-judge [yishpot], for [there is] a-time for-every matter [le-khol chefetz] and-for every work [ma'aseh] there."

**3:18** I-said, I, in-my-heart concerning the-matter of-the-sons of-the-human, that God is-testing-them [le-varam ha-Elohim], and-to-see [ve-li-r'ot] that they [are] beasts [behemah] — they in-themselves [hemmah la-hem].

**3:19** For the-fate [miqreh] of-the-sons of-the-human and-the-fate of-the-beast [ha-behemah] — one fate [miqreh echad] [is] to-them: as-the-death of-this, so [is] the-death of-that, and-one breath [ruach echad] [is] to-all; and-the-advantage [motar] of-the-human over the-beast [is] nothing [ayin], for the-all [is] vapor [havel].

**3:20** The-all goes to one place [maqom echad]: the-all was from the-dust [ha-afar], and-the-all returns to the-dust. **3:21** Who knows [mi yode'a] the-breath [ruach] of-the-sons of-the-human — does-it-go-up [ha-olah hi] to-above [le-ma'alah], and-the-breath of-the-beast — does-it-go-down [ha-yoredet hi] to-below [le-mattah] to-the-earth [la-aretz]?

**3:22** And-I-saw that-there-is-nothing [ein] good [tov] except that the-human [ha-adam] should-rejoice [yismach] in-his-works [be-ma'asav], for that [is] his-portion [chelqo]. For who will-bring-him [yevi'ennu] to-see what will-be after-him [acharav]?

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.11 — ha-olam:** This word can mean "eternity," "the world," or "obscurity/hiddenness." God has placed *ha-olam* in the human heart — a sense of something beyond the moment — yet humans cannot grasp the full scope of God's work. The tension between longing and limitation is the theological center of Ecclesiastes.

**v.15 — "God seeks the pursued":** The Hebrew *et-nirdaf* (the pursued/persecuted one) is enigmatic. Does God pursue what has fled (time)? Or does God seek out the oppressed? The ambiguity is likely intentional.

**v.21 — "Who knows?":** The Masoretic vocalization makes this a genuine question, not a denial. Qohelet does not say the human spirit does *not* rise — he asks who can *know* that it does. This is epistemic humility, not materialism.

*-- EMET*
